# Northvale has frozen withdrawals. Here’s what happened — and what we’re doing

**10 November 2026 · By Inês, Product Designer at Pinha**

All dates below are 2026.

I’m Inês. I work on product design at Pinha — I write a lot of the small text you see in the app. I’m writing this post because Rui is spending today on calls with lawyers and Banco de Portugal, and because I’m too angry to let this go out as a corporate statement.

I’m furious at Northvale. I’m also angry at us for trusting them the way we did. You deserve a clear explanation, not a polished one.

## The short version

- On **6 November at 09:00**, Northvale Payments froze **all withdrawals** from Pinha without warning. Deposits and round-ups stopped too.
- Your money is **not lost**. It is held in a safeguarded account, separate from Northvale’s own money. Northvale cannot use it.
- But we cannot move it until Northvale releases it.
- We have already signed a new payments partner, **Ostra Bank in Lisbon**. The migration needs Northvale to send the balances file and Banco de Portugal to give approval. Our estimate is **10 to 15 working days**. That is an estimate, **not a promise**.
- We filed complaints with **Banco de Portugal** and the **Lithuanian central bank** on **7 November**.
- The monthly fee is cancelled for **November and December for everyone**.
- If your case is urgent — rent, medical, losing your job — email **urgent@pinha.example** with the subject **URGENTE**.

## What actually happened

Northvale Payments is an e-money institution based in Vilnius. They hold customer money in a safeguarded account. That means the money is kept separate from Northvale’s own money, and Northvale cannot use it for its own business. That part is important. It is also the maddening part: the money is protected from Northvale, but you can’t get to it because Northvale controls the account.

On **4 November**, Northvale emailed us a “commercial termination” with 30 days’ notice. No real reason. Just a “risk appetite review”.

On **6 November at 09:00**, they blocked all outgoing transfers. No warning. That was against what their own notice said. Deposits and round-ups stopped as well.

They gave us 30 days and then blocked everything less than two days later. I’m not going to call that a risk review. It’s cowardice.

On **Friday 6 November**, their account manager stopped answering our calls. The phone now goes to a voicemail in Lithuanian.

We filed complaints with Banco de Portugal and the Lithuanian central bank on **7 November**. Rui is on calls today with lawyers and Banco de Portugal. We are not sitting still.

## What this means for your money

Your money is still your money. It is not lost. It is sitting in a safeguarded account, and Northvale cannot use it.

But I’m not going to pretend you can access it today. You can’t. Not until Northvale releases it. That is the situation, and I hate it.

We have signed with Ostra Bank in Lisbon. That is real progress. But migration is not just switching a logo. It needs two things: Northvale has to send the balances file, and Banco de Portugal has to give approval. We estimate **10 to 15 working days** once those things happen. I’m not giving you a fixed date, because I’m not going to promise a date I can’t keep. If it slips, I’ll tell you it slipped. I won’t bury it.

## Our mistake

Let me be direct about our part.

We built Pinha with one payments partner and no real backup. That was naive. It was our mistake, and I’m saying it plainly. You trusted us to hold your money in a way you could get to. We trusted Northvale to behave like a regulated partner. Both of those things failed.

I’m not going to hide behind “industry practice” or “unforeseen circumstances”. We should have had a second path before this happened. We didn’t. That is on us.

## The screen I designed

I designed the screen in the app that says: **“Your money is always yours. Take it out anytime.”**

I looked at it this weekend and felt sick. It wasn’t a lie when I wrote it. It was what we believed. But I understand why it feels like one now. I’m not going to delete it and pretend it never existed. I want it to be true again.

On Saturday I read a message from a customer in Porto. She wrote in all capitals. She had saved for three years for a car deposit. The stand gives her until **Friday, 13 November**. I read it on the metro and nearly cried.

I’m not putting her name here. But I want her to know I read it, and that it is not just a support ticket to me. I can’t promise her deadline will be saved. I can promise we are trying.

If you are in a situation like hers, use the urgent email below.

## What you can do now

**1. If your case is urgent, email us.**
Rent, medical, losing your job, or another deadline that can’t wait: write to **urgent@pinha.example** with the subject **URGENTE**. Tell us the email on your Pinha account and what the deadline is. We are trying to get individual releases from Northvale for these cases. I can’t promise every one will succeed, but we are pushing hard.

**2. If you’ve already written to support, we have it.**
We’ve had **1,900 support emails since Friday 6 November**. Our team is three people. Reply time is around **two days** right now. If you’re waiting, that’s why. We are not ignoring you.

**3. Your monthly fee is cancelled for November and December.**
For everyone. You don’t need to ask.

**4. Deposits and round-ups are stopped.**
You can’t add money right now. That is Northvale, not us choosing to block you.

**5. Check the blog.**
We will post updates every **Monday and Thursday** until this is solved. The next one will be Thursday.

## What happens next

We are pushing Northvale to release the balances file. We are pushing Banco de Portugal for approval. We are working with Ostra Bank on the migration. We are handling urgent cases one by one where we can.

I’m not going to tell you to calm down. You deserve to be angry. At Northvale, and at us. Keep asking questions. We’ll keep answering as fast as three people can, and we’ll keep posting every Monday and Thursday until this is fixed.

I’m sorry. Not in the “we apologise for any inconvenience” way. In the way where I designed the screen that says your money is yours, and I can’t make it work today.

**Inês**
Product Designer, Pinha
